intent_contract.text: Requester asks for independent randomly complex concepts to test the newly integrated hair topic using the attached portrait. The raw request contains delivery instructions and broad visual scope only. Arm C independently proposes the rain-arrival planetarium repair moment: a technician must keep the hair clear of a fragile star disc, so lifting the dark outer panel reveals the pale inner layer. The same hair carries dry crown sheen and damp tip clumping. The viewer should first read this layered color/material contrast, then the softly attentive face, then the interrupted repair. Scene, hair colors, moisture distribution, clothing, gestures, camera and all five test conditions are agent choices, not requester definitions or biographical claims. An independent random draw selected the circumstance. Saved sensual=1 is a subtle supporting human presence; fetish=0 adds no focused erotic treatment, creativity=1 develops restrained plausible variations, surreal=0 keeps ordinary physical causality, and resolved sensual-led emphasis remains secondary to the hair experiment. An outdoor hood protected the crown while exposed tips acquired rain. A night-club hair display was considered but rejected because colored illumination would obscure the local-color test; a mirror salon display was less causally connected than the repair moment.

A photographic portrait of one woman in a working pause at a planetarium repair bench. Retain the visible facial impression from the supplied portrait: softly oval face, large dark eyes, gently arched brows, a small straight nose, and softly parted lips. This is a fictional working scene, with the hair designed for this photograph. She stands beside a dismantled star projector, wearing an ivory cotton work shirt with an open collar and a slate apron. Her right fingertips steady the rim of a perforated brass star disc already resting flat in its circular cradle; its empty lamp housing and a small screwdriver make the unfinished repair readable. A wet hooded raincoat draped over the chair and droplets on the window link her arrival to the rain outside. Her shoulder-length hair has a deep coffee-brown outer mantle over a pale neutral-silver underlayer. The dark top panel covers the crown and upper side of her head. Her left fingertips gently lift this dark outer panel backward just above her left ear, opening a broad window onto the silver hair growing underneath at the ear and nape. The lifted brown edge visibly overlaps the silver inner panel; that silver panel continues downward to her shoulder, retaining its bright diffuse color along its length. The near-side overlap and the separated tips are clearly readable. The silver stays pale even where it receives diffuse light, while the brown remains dark between its narrow reflections. Her protected crown is dry, smoothly combed, and satin-glossy, with fine separated strands and a narrow controlled reflection tracing the brown curve. Only the lowest three centimeters of both colored layers remain damp from the rain: those tips group into small irregular strand clusters, with tiny distinct water beads suspended on several ends. The dry smooth crown and damp clustered ends are visible together. She keeps her lifted hand clear of the exposed inner panel and glances toward the camera with quiet warmth, as though acknowledging a colleague before returning to the disc. Her expression and relaxed open collar provide a subtle human attraction that supports the working moment. Frame from a little above the entire crown to the lower bench edge in a vertical medium close-up, from her left-front three-quarter direction at eye height. Keep the complete hair silhouette, left ear, revealed inner panel, shoulder-length ends, both connected forearms, and supported brass disc in view. A large neutral-white diffused task light beside the lens gives consistent local hair color and a soft facial transition; the dim planetarium and its unlit dome recede behind her. Use a natural 55 mm photographic perspective and enough depth of field for the crown, layer boundary, water beads, and fingertips to be sharp. The hair color relationship is the first read, her attentive face the second, and the interrupted repair the third.
